advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that offloads a tool taking a keyword argument and asserts the offloaded call returns the correct value for that argument (argument passthrough through _thread_offloaded).
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:166-169: `async def _offloaded(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any: ... return await anyio.to_thread.run_sync(functools.partial(fn, *args, **kwargs))`

src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:160-163 docstring: 'the SDK already built this tool's fn_metadata ... and Tool.run passes arguments by KEYWORD, so the wrapper must stay transparent to introspection and accept whatever the original accepted'

All four call_tool sites pass no arguments: tests/unit/test_mcp_tool_offload.py:70, :131, :194, :222 each use `call_tool(<name>, {})`; the tool bodies slow_sync/read_marker/review_plan take zero parameters

ABSENCE: no test defines an offloaded tool with a parameter (e.g. `def echo(text: str) -> str: return text`) and asserts `call_tool('echo', {'text': 'hi'})` returns 'hi', so the *args/**kwargs forwarding and post-wraps arg validation are unverified
advisory.finding: The new _thread_offloaded wrapper's argument passthrough (functools.partial(fn, *args, **kwargs) plus functools.wraps for the SDK's keyword-argument model) is never exercised: every test offloads and calls a zero-parameter tool with call_tool(name, {}). A tool that takes arguments could break passthrough or argument-model introspection undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test defining `@mcp.tool() def echo(text: str) -> str: return text`, run offload_sync_tools(mcp), then assert `anyio.run(...)` of `call_tool('echo', {'text': 'hi'})` yields 'hi', proving *args/**kwargs are forwarded and the SDK's keyword arg model still validates after wrapping.

evidence: Commit message: 'concurrent store writes are already excluded by the store lock's mkdir leg, which is atomic between threads' — an assertion, with no test in tests/unit/test_mcp_tool_offload.py exercising two write tools running concurrently.

ABSENCE: the new test file only ever runs one tool concurrently with a non-tool coroutine (_call_while_something_else_runs starts run_tool + concurrent_request); no test runs two offloaded tool bodies at once to confirm shared-state / store-write safety under the new concurrency.
advisory.finding: offload_sync_tools converts every sync tool body from serialized event-loop execution to concurrent worker-thread execution (bounded by anyio's default ~40-slot limiter). Tool bodies that previously could rely on implicit single-threaded serialization now run concurrently; the diff's only stated safety argument is the store lock's atomic mkdir leg, which is asserted but not verified in this change nor exercised by the new tests.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and document whether offloaded tool bodies should be cancellable (abandon_on_cancel) and confirm the SIGTERM drain interacts correctly with non-cancellable worker threads.
evidence: anyio.to_thread.run_sync defaults to abandon_on_cancel=False, meaning a cancel of the awaiting coroutine does not stop the worker thread — it detaches only if cancellable/abandon_on_cancel is True

The module already owns a bounded SIGTERM drain (drain_then_exit / make_sigterm_handler) whose semantics assume in-flight work eventually completes; a non-cancellable multi-minute body is exactly the work that can outrun the grace window
dropped.finding: anyio.to_thread.run_sync is invoked with its default cancellable=False (abandon_on_cancel=False), so a tool body offloaded to a worker thread cannot be cancelled once started; if the ASGI request coroutine is cancelled (client disconnect, uvicorn graceful shutdown, or the SIGTERM path setting should_exit) the worker thread runs to completion regardless. A 177-second list_tickets or 15-20 minute review_plan will keep occupying a limiter slot and mint/finish work after the request is gone, and the SIGTERM grace drain will still be waiting on it.
scenarios: Client disconnects mid-call during a 177s list_tickets
SIGTERM arrives while a review_plan body is running on a worker thread

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Have wire_health log the offloaded count (and/or warn when _tool_manager is absent) so a zero-offload run is distinguishable from a correctly-offloaded one.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:187-189: `manager = getattr(mcp, "_tool_manager", None)` / `if manager is None:` / `return 0` — a missing manager is indistinguishable from a legitimately empty/all-async server
The count is only asserted in unit tests; in production wire_health neither logs nor checks it, so an absent tool manager produces the same visible result as a correctly-offloaded server
dropped.finding: wire_health discards the return value of offload_sync_tools, so when the server has no _tool_manager (or no sync tools), the offload silently no-ops with no log or signal — the same fail-open shape as instrument_certified_tools. A build that failed to register tools would serve with bodies still on the loop and nothing distinguishes 'offloaded 0 because all async' from 'offloaded 0 because manager missing'.
scenarios: A build where LLM tools were not registered / _tool_manager attribute contract changed
